extracted.intended_audience: trial investigators, trial designers, funders, research ethics committees/IRBs, journal editors, peer reviewers, trial registries, policymakers, regulators, patients and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting the minimum content of protocols for randomized trials (primarily two‑group parallel designs) to ensure transparency, reproducibility, oversight and adequate reporting. The checklist specifies items that should be addressed in a protocol, supporting review by funders, REC/IRBs, journals and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a randomized trial protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol is a central document that provides sufficient detail to enable (1) understanding of the rationale, objectives, population, interventions, methods, statistical analyses, ethical considerations, dissemination plans and administration of the trial; (2) replication of trial methods and conduct; and (3) appraisal of trial validity, feasibility and ethical rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full protocol must be submitted for approval by an REC/IRB before enrolling participants. The protocol is a living document and every version should contain a transparent audit trail documenting dates and descriptions of changes. Important amendments should be reported to REC/IRBs and trial registries as they occur and described in reports of completed trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration (open science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include trial registration information, including date of trial registration (Item 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial registration is part of the new open science section and is critical to promoting access to information about trial methods and results. Ensure registry record is consistent with the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to full protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify where the full protocol and the statistical analysis plan can be accessed (Item 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist calls for making the protocol and SAP available (e.g. via trial registry, journal, or repository) to support transparency and reproducibility. Related documents should be referenced in the protocol and made available for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans for sharing de-identified participant-level data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for sharing de-identified participant-level data (Item 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the open science section; indicate what data will be shared, timing, access conditions and how privacy/confidentiality will be protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and conflicts of interest (open science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose funding sources and conflicts of interest, including financial and other conflicts of interest of steering committee members (Item 7 and 7b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make funding and COI information explicit in the protocol; align with Declaration of Helsinki and other ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination policy and authorship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide plans for dissemination of trial results and policies on authorship eligibility and use of professional writers (Item 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 8 now merges dissemination policy and authorship guidelines — specify how and when results will be shared and criteria for authorship. If an item is not relevant, explicitly state and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and public involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how patients and the public are involved in the design, conduct, and reporting of the trial (Item 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of PPI activities and how input influenced trial design or conduct; report PPI contributors' roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial monitoring (replaces auditing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe trial monitoring arrangements (Item 29), noting that this replaces the prior checklist item on auditing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the monitoring plan (who, frequency, scope), how monitoring differs from auditing, and plans for oversight of safety and data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding: who and how; similarity of interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: State who will be blinded and how (Item 24a/24b); include description of the similarity of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split into sub‑items: (a) who will be blinded (participants, care providers, outcome assessors, data analysts) and (b) how blinding will be achieved; describe measures to ensure interventions appear similar when blinding is planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and assessment of harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how harms/adverse events will be assessed and reported (items integrated from CONSORT Harms 2022 — items 10, 17, 27a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on definitions, collection methods, timing, severity grading, attribution, analysis and reporting of harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of interventions and comparators (TIDieR integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed information on interventions and comparators (Item 15a) in line with TIDieR guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include content, dosage, mode of delivery, timing, personnel involved, fidelity and any measures to ensure replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for participants, sites and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify eligibility criteria for (a) participants and (b) sites and personnel (Item 14a/b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define inclusion/exclusion criteria for people, and criteria for selecting sites and trial staff to facilitate reproducibility and appraisal of generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis population and handling of missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the analysis population and methods for handling missing data (Items 27b/27c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State primary analysis population (e.g., intention-to-treat, per-protocol), rules for inclusion/exclusion in analyses, and predefined strategies for missing data (imputation methods, sensitivity analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specify planned sensitivity analyses (Item 27d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which sensitivity analyses will be performed to assess robustness of primary findings and handling of key assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and access to data
rubrics_metrics.description: Document data management procedures and access to data (merged item 26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data collection processes, quality control, storage, backup, retention, ownership and who will have access to the dataset (including external access provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of enrolment, interventions and assessments (diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a diagram illustrating the schedule of enrolment, interventions and assessments for trial participants (Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the timetable/flow diagram to make timing of enrolment, interventions and outcome assessments explicit and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and sample size calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sample size rationale and calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assumptions (effect size, variance, power, alpha), any planned interim analyses that affect sample size, and justification for chosen parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (primary and secondary) definition and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define primary and secondary outcomes and how they will be measured and analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise definitions, measurement instruments, timing, units, and plans for outcome derivation and handling of multiple outcomes or multiplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation sequence generation and concealment (randomization methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe treatment allocation methods and processes to generate and conceal the allocation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe randomization method, sequence generation, stratification or minimization, allocation concealment mechanisms and who implements/randomizes participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of adverse events (safety monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify methods for detecting and recording adverse events and safety outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include definitions, surveillance methods, timing, reporting lines, and relationship to monitoring and data safety oversight committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods and analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe planned statistical methods for primary and secondary analyses and reference the full statistical analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline primary analysis models, covariates, subgroup analyses, interim analyses, multiplicity adjustments, and links to the available SAP document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of sponsors and investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe roles of sponsors, investigators, and other contributors in trial design, conduct, analysis, reporting and data access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify responsibilities to avoid undisclosed influence; include agreements on publication rights, data ownership and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol amendments and versioning (audit trail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a transparent audit trail for protocol versions documenting dates and descriptions of changes; report important amendments to REC/IRBs and trial registries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments are tracked and communicated; describe processes for making and approving amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of protocols and related documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Make full protocols and related documents publicly available through trial registries, journals, or repositories where feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability enhances transparency, facilitates appraisal and allows comparison with publications to detect selective reporting or undisclosed amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of a completed SPIRIT 2025 checklist with protocol submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting protocols for review or publication, include a completed SPIRIT 2025 checklist indicating where checklist items are reported in the protocol (e.g., page numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reviewers and editors check completeness; if an item is not relevant, explicitly state that and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency across protocol, related documents and trial registry
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the information in the protocol, related documents (e.g., SAP, data management plan) and trial registry record is consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies can obscure planned methods and facilitate selective reporting; cross‑reference related documents in the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability (focus on two‑group parallel trials but general relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT 2025 addresses minimum content focusing on the two-group parallel randomized trial but most items are relevant to other trial types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the checklist is a minimum standard; for specific designs/extensions (e.g., factorial, PROs, AI, dose-finding) consult relevant SPIRIT extensions.
